country.comment: Study examines two Public Water Supply Districts in Missouri (Boone County PWSD No. 5 and Barton County PWSD No. 1) in 'Mid-America', referencing U.S. federal credit via the Farmers Home Administration and USDA (Washington, D.C.).
country.where_found: PDF p. 3 (journal p. 95), Historical Backdrop and The Problem; PDF p. 4 (journal p. 96), Overview of Districts Studied

effect_estimate.comment: All reported figures are descriptive sample percentages and means from self-reported mail survey responses without inferential hypothesis tests, standard errors, or non-district household survey controls.
effect_estimate.value: Initiation of Public Water Supply District (PWSD) service eliminated reliance on hauled water in both districts: in rural-urban fringe Boone County PWSD No. 5 (n = 211 respondents), 33% previously bought hauled water at $5.57/1,000 gallons (privately pumped water cost $1.54/1,000 gallons), district water averaged $2.22/1,000 gallons, and mean monthly water consumption rose 37% from 2,218 to 3,031 gallons/month; in agricultural Barton County PWSD No. 1 (n = 448 respondents), 40% previously used hauled water at $2.10/1,000 gallons (privately pumped water cost $1.21/1,000 gallons, district water cost roughly $2.10/1,000 gallons), and mean monthly consumption per connection rose from 4,283 to 4,708 gallons/month. Post-PWSD in-migration accounted for 82 respondents (40%) in Boone No. 5 (21% citing district water as a migration factor) and 112 respondents (25%) in Barton No. 1 (13% citing district water); home improvement outlays averaged $1,126 (n = 25) in Boone No. 5 and $672 in Barton No. 1, and self-estimated land values rose 77% ($274 to $484/acre) in Boone No. 5 and 21% (n = 66) in Barton No. 1 (descriptive statistics only; no confidence intervals or p-values reported).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 5-8 (journal pp. 97-100), Impacts Registered in the Rural-Urban Fringe District, Impacts in the Agricultural District, and Summary of Findings

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling for a descriptive cross-sectional survey appraised with JBI is 2. Rated 1 (documented descriptive association) because the survey documents pre/post changes in formal piped water use, water unit costs, and consumption following creation of statutory PWSDs, whereas administrative/planning mechanisms (e.g., Regional Planning Commission construction authorization operating as a formality and lack of community-wide locational planning causing strip development) are discussed as institutional context or explicitly noted as not directly investigated empirically.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 2 (journal p. 94), Abstract; PDF p. 3 (journal p. 95), Historical Backdrop, The Problem, and Footnote 1; PDF pp. 5-8 (journal pp. 97-100)

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines statutory Public Water Supply District formation and spatial distribution-line boundaries in rural vs. rural-urban fringe areas (ELIGIBILITY: service_area), Regional Planning Commission construction authorization and the reliance on engineering feasibility studies rather than community-wide locational planning (ELIGIBILITY: planning), and district water charges per 1,000 gallons relative to private/hauled alternatives (BURDEN: fees).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2 (journal p. 94), Abstract; PDF p. 3 (journal p. 95), Historical Backdrop, The Problem, and Footnote 1; PDF pp. 5-7 (journal pp. 97-99); PDF p. 9 (journal p. 101), Conclusions

outcome_flags.comment: Measures transition from private wells/cisterns and hauled water to formal PWSD piped connections (formal_connection, water_access), monthly water consumption per household/connection in gallons (service_quantity), and unit cost per 1,000 gallons across hauled, privately pumped, and district water (affordability).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 4 (journal p. 96), Overview of Districts Studied; PDF pp. 5-8 (journal pp. 97-100)

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary quantitative cross-sectional mail survey of members in two water districts with retrospective recall items and descriptive comparisons across the two district types; lacks a non-district household control group or quasi-experimental identification strategy required for ROBINS-I.
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies

sample_size.comment: Mail questionnaires were sent to all members in both selected districts, with an overall reported return rate of approximately 65% in each district (211 of 317 families in Boone County PWSD No. 5; 448 of 700 families in Barton County PWSD No. 1; item-specific response counts vary, e.g., 66 respondents estimating land value appreciation in Barton County).
sample_size.value: 2 Public Water Supply Districts serving 1,017 families total (659 mail questionnaire respondents: 211 respondents of 317 families in Boone County PWSD No. 5; 448 respondents of 700 families in Barton County PWSD No. 1)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 3 (journal p. 95), Footnote 2; PDF p. 4 (journal p. 96), Rural-Urban Fringe District and Agricultural District; PDF p. 7 (journal p. 99), Impacts in the Agricultural District

study_design.comment: Purposive selection of two Missouri PWSDs (one rural-urban fringe, operational April 1967; one agricultural, operational October 1968) surveyed via a single post-initiation mail questionnaire asking members for retrospective before-and-after figures on water sources, costs, consumption, in-migration, home improvements, and self-estimated land values, analyzed with descriptive percentages and means.
study_design.value: Comparative cross-sectional mail questionnaire survey of members in two purposively selected Public Water Supply Districts (descriptive ex-post analysis)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 3 (journal p. 95), The Problem and Footnote 2; PDF pp. 4-5 (journal pp. 96-97), Overview of Districts Studied and Comparison of Districts
